text:
maya: heads up — after the eu->us spill tests last night i see a latency tail popping in eu-prod around 99th pct for small requests (<=64 tokens). suspecting our eager batching/priority logic + kv cache churn. anyone else seeing this?

jordan: saw the metric too. looks correlated with cross-zone routing when eu pool is near capacity and requests spill to us. 99p jumps ~80ms on top of baseline.

sasha: quick note: kernel selection didn't change in that deploy. this smells like batch formation timing and token budget targets causing more KV cache invalidations on the EU nodes.

liam: i profiled one of the EU backends at 02:20 UTC. sample traces show more short-lived batches (2-3 requests) instead of the usual 6-8, and a lot of KV cache misses immediately after a spill-back. attaching a small snippet of the profiler output: 

```
# hot-path excerpts
batch_size_hist: {1: 41, 2: 128, 3: 97, 6: 32}
kv_cache_hit_rate: 0.62 -> baseline 0.89
kernel_selection: llama2-7b-int8 (same)
cpu_latency_ms: +12
```

anita: interesting — if spill decisions are too eager, they might be forcing requests onto remote nodes that don't have warmed KV caches, and our token-budget target is small so we flush cached k-v entries more often.

maya: here's the current queue policy config we use for regional dispatch: 

```
queue_policy:
  mode: priority-preferred
  spill_threshold: 0.85
  eagerness: 0.9
  token_budget_target: 128
  min_batch_delay_ms: 6
  cross_zone_affinity: soft
```

jordan: two ideas: 1) reduce eagerness so we prefer short local queues until latency SLO breached, 2) bump token_budget_target for EU to reduce eviction churn.

sasha: +1 for region-specific token targets. EU traffic profile is short request heavy (chat + tools calls) — we can set token_budget_target=256 for eu and 96 for us, experiment window 4 hours.

liam: tested locally in canary with token_budget_target=256 and eagerness=0.75. result: batch_size mean went from 3.1 -> 4.9, kv hit rate 0.62 -> 0.81, 99p reduced ~55ms. still need to watch host-level burst capacity cost.

anita: tradeoff: increasing token_budget increases memory use per queue and might raise p99 under pathological long-seq loads. we should couple with a per-model cap (eg model_max_kv_mb).

maya: agree. propose we run a 6hr canary in eu region with following overrides: 

```
overrides:
  region: eu
  queue_policy:
    eagerness: 0.75
    spill_threshold: 0.9
    token_budget_target: 256
    cross_zone_affinity: hard
  model_limits:
    model_max_kv_mb: 1600
```

jordan: can we also add a short-circuit in the router so that if remote routing would add >20ms network RTT we keep local but degrade batch size target first? avoids cold-kv penalty.

sasha: yes — add a rule: if estimated_net_rtt + expected_kv_warm_penalty > local_delay_budget then prefer local. Pseudocode: 

```
if (rtt_remote + kv_warm_penalty > local_delay_budget) {
  route_local()
} else {
  route_remote()
}
```

liam: i can instrument kv_warm_penalty as 40ms for eu->us based on today's traces, and wire that into the router cost model.

anita: quick thought on metrics: add kv_cache_miss_origin tag (local|remote) so we can tell whether misses are due to routing or local churn.

maya: good idea. also add batch_formation_latency and batch_wait_time per region. need to track token eviction counts too.

deploy-bot: deploy queued: eu-canary/queue-policy-override @maya requested — ETA 7m.

jordan: once canary is up, let's run a synthetic workload that mimics 60% short chat, 30% medium instructions, 10% long. capture 1h baseline before/after.

sasha: setting alert: if eu 99p > baseline+70ms for >5m, auto-rollback the canary.

liam: one more caveat: kernel profiling shows a small reg in attention kernel performance when batch sizes exceed 12 on the newer hosts. so we should cap batch shaping to avoid single-host huge batches while trying to increase avg batch size. add max_batch_size=10 per node.

anita: noted. that cap mitigates kernel regression risk.

maya: plan summary: run eu canary with overrides above, wire in router short-circuit, add metrics (kv_cache_miss_origin, batch_formation_latency, token_evictions), cap max_batch_size=10. monitor 1h synthetic + live traffic, rollback if p99 reg. i'll own canary and post results. :thumbsup:

jordan: thanks. ping @sasha if we need quick kernel rollback knobs.

sasha: standing by.

maya: posting results in this thread after 1h.
